edits.english: The mishna teaches: If the gentile hired the Jew to do other work with him, even if the gentile said to the Jew while he was working with him: Transport the barrel of libation wine for me from this place to that place, the Jew's wage is permitted. The Gemara notes that this formulation of the mishna indicates that this wage is permitted even if the gentile did not say to the Jew to transport the barrel of wine toward evening, meaning, toward the end of his workday.

edits.hebrew: ואע"ג – דהעברת חבית לאו לעיתותי ערב, לאחר שנשלם כל זמן שכר פעולתו, אלא קודם גמר זמן שכירותו אמר לו: העבר חבית של יין נסך. קתני מתניתין: שכרו מותר? בתמיה!

edits.english: We learned in the Mishna that if the gentile hired the Jew to do other work with him, and during his work, the gentile told him to transport a barrel of libation wine for him — his wage is permitted. And they comment: And from the general wording of the Mishna, it is to be understood that the law is so even if the gentile did not say to him this thing toward evening, meaning, at the end of the workday.

In Tosafot and other Rishonim, they discussed the question of why we do not say that our Mishna follows the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who holds that in any such case, everything is permitted except for the value of the libation wine itself, or according to the view of Rabbi Eliezer, who says that one can take from the money an amount equivalent to the value of one barrel and throw it into the sea, and the rest is permitted. Primarily, they explained that they wished to establish the Mishna according to everyone's opinion, and not as the words of individuals (even in a case where some hold that the *halakha* follows them). And also, that the Mishna here is concise in its words and does not differentiate, implying that the entire wage is permitted.

Rashi explains that it is after the employer had already become obligated to pay the Jew his entire wage before the transporting of that barrel. And in the Turid, it is written that 'toward evening' is not precise, but rather even in the middle of the day, if the work for which he was hired was completed. And similarly, if the gentile hired him to do completely different work and asked him to transport a barrel of libation wine, it is certainly not the time that is the cause, but rather the fact that the matter is part of the work for which he was hired. And the Rashba wrote (in Torat HaBayit) that 'toward evening' is mentioned here because it refers to someone hired as a laborer for a day's work (and not specifically for this task of transporting barrels), and the novelty is that even though he was hired for the entire day, since there was no time left in the day to do this work — it is not included in the hiring.

And the Gemara raises a contradiction from a baraita: In the case of one who hires a laborer, and toward evening the employer said to the laborer: Transport this barrel of libation wine from this place to that place, his wage is permitted. By inference, the reason for this ruling is that the employer said it to the laborer toward evening, and therefore yes, it is permitted, as it is clear that the laborer has completed the labor for which he is being paid and the wage is not for moving the barrel. But if this happened during the entire day, not toward evening, this would not be permitted.

edits.hebrew: ולעיתותי ערב – דכבר נתחייב לו כל שכרו קודם העברת חבית.

edits.english: And the Gemara raises a contradiction from what we learned in a *baraita*: If a gentile hires a laborer, and toward evening the gentile said to him: "Transport a barrel of libation wine from place to place" — his wage is permitted. And we infer from there: The reason is specifically when the gentile said to him toward evening — yes, the law is so, that it is permitted, because it is clear that the laborer completed the work for which he receives his wage, and the transporting of this barrel is not related to that. But if he did so during the entire day — no!

Meaning, the wage for that day's work that was done permissibly. And the Rishonim brought from the Tosefta that *ab initio* it is forbidden to do this work of transporting the barrel with him toward evening. And see in the Rashba, who understood that the intention is that even for free, the matter is forbidden, for anything done toward evening has no wage but rather a benefit, and despite this, the matter is forbidden because the Jew desires its continued existence so that the gentile will owe him this favor (see above 63b regarding one who was hired to break a barrel of libation wine). And in the Yerushalmi, they said that if he did it for a benefit, they seize from the laborer's property an amount equivalent to the wage for that work.

edits.hebrew: טעמא דא"ל לעיתותי ערב כו' – הא דלא משני מתניתין כרשב"ג דאמר: ימכר כולו חוץ מדמי יין נסך, וכאן נמי שכרו מותר חוץ מדמי חבית. דניחא ליה לאוקמי כרבנן. אי נמי: שכרו מותר משמע כל שכרו. אי נמי בהא, אפילו רבן שמעון בן גמליאל מודי. דהתם אין דרך ליקח יין מן העובד כוכבים, והכא דרך בני אדם ליקח שכר מן העובד כוכבים, ויש לאסור כל השכר. וחילוק זה יש בירושלמי. ולעיל סוף פרק כל הצלמים (עבודה זרה דף מט:) גבי ארג בו את הבגד. ולפי התירוץ דניחא לאוקמא כרבנן, ניחא דלא תיקשי: נוקמה כר"א דאית ליה לעיל יש פדיון לעבודת כוכבים ויוליך הנאה לים המלח אף בלא זה וזה גורם, וקיימא לן כוותיה. ולתירוץ האחר נמי יש לומר: שכרו מותר משמע בלא פדיון.

edits.english: Abaye said: When we learned this in the mishna as well, we learned this with regard to the case where the employer said this toward evening. Rava said: This is not difficult. This case, where the wage is forbidden if it was not toward evening, is a case where the gentile employer said to the laborer: Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot, in which case moving all of the barrels is considered a single task, and if one of the barrels was libation wine, the entire wage is forbidden. That case, in which the wage is permitted in any event, is a case where the employer said to the laborer: Transport each barrel for me for one peruta, such that each barrel is its own task.

edits.hebrew: רבא אמר – לעולם דלא אמר ליה לעיתותי ערב.

ולא קשיא – מתניתין דקתני מותר, כגון: העבר לי חבית בפרוטה, ונמצאת חבית של יין נסך ביניהן, שדי פרוטה לנהרא, או לא שקיל מיד עובד כוכבים, ואינך משתרו, דהא לא שייך שכר ההוא חבית בהדי אינך, דכל חדא קנין אגרא באפי נפשא. וברייתא דכי לא אמר ליה לעיתותי ערב הוי כל שכרו אסור, כגון דאמר ליה: העבר ק' חביות בק' פרוטות, דכל כמה דלא אעברינהו לכולהו לא יהיב ליה מידי, הלכך כולי אגרא שייך ביה.

edits.english: Abaye said: When we learned our Mishna as well, we learned it in a case where the employer said this toward evening. Rava said: This is not difficult. This case, where the wage is forbidden if it was not toward evening, is a case where the employer said to the laborer: "Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot," for then the transporting of all the barrels is considered one task, and if one of them was libation wine, the entire wage is forbidden due to the wage for libation wine being mixed in. That case, where it is permitted in any event — is a case where the employer said to the laborer: "Transport each barrel for me for one peruta," where the wage for each barrel is paid individually.

And so it is taught in a baraita: In the case of one who hires a laborer and said to the laborer: Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot, and a barrel of libation wine was found among them, his wage is forbidden. But if the employer said to the laborer: Transport each barrel for one peruta, and there was a barrel of libation wine among them, his wage is permitted.

If a gentile hired a laborer and said to him: 'Transport one hundred barrels of liquor for me for one hundred perutot,' and one of them was found to be wine, his entire wage is forbidden, since there is among them the value of one peruta from the wage for libation wine. If it was less than the value of one peruta, it is permitted *ex post facto*. And if he said to him: 'Transport each barrel for one peruta,' and a barrel of wine was found among them, the wage for that barrel of wine is forbidden, and the rest of his wage is permitted. However, *ab initio* it is forbidden to do so.

And so it is taught in a *baraita*: One who hires a laborer, and said to him: "Transport one hundred barrels for me for one hundred perutot," and one barrel of libation wine was found among them — his wage is forbidden due to this mixture. But if he said to him: "Each barrel for one peruta," and a barrel of libation wine was found among them — his wage is permitted.

edits.hebrew: הא דאמר ליה העבר לי ק' חביות בק' פרוטות – ובהא אסרה ברייתא כי לא אמר לו לעיתותי ערב, דכל כמה דלא אעברינהו לכולהו לא יהיב ליה מידי, הלכך כוליה אגרא שייך ביה. כן לשון הקונט' משמע. הא אמר ליה לעיתותי ערב מותר, ואע"ג שהיא מאותם חביות שהתנה עמו. וקשה, דמ"מ שכר האיסור מעורב בכל ההיתר. לכן נראה לפרש: ולעיתותי ערב, אחר שהשלים קבלנותו, אמר לו כן. ואשמעינן שאע"פ שלא עשה עמו תנאי חדש, אלא על פי תנאי הראשון הוא מעביר בפרוטה לפי חשבון מאה במאה פרוטות, וסלקא דעתך שהכל שכר אחד הוא ונמצא בשכרו מעורב שכר יין נסך. קא משמע לן דשרי, והוה ליה כמעביר ביום של אחריו מאחר שכבר השלים קבלנותו.
